channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: WHO urges Afghanistan to resume house-to-house polio vaccinations amid rising cases
item.description: The World Health Organization is pressing Afghanistan to reinstate house-to-house polio vaccination campaigns. The country has reported 25 wild polio cases this year, exceeding last year's total. WHO warns that the current system of fixed vaccination sites is failing to reach many children, increasing the risk of further spread.

item.title: Trump discusses US policy on Iran, Cuba, and relations with Israel
item.description: In a media interview, President Trump outlined US policy towards Iran and Cuba, and discussed relations with Israel. He affirmed strong support for Israel and expressed readiness to use military force to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons, not ruling out renewed large-scale operations. Trump also aims to resolve issues with Cuba before his term ends.

item.title: Uzbekistan Joins $720 Million International Climate Investment Program
item.description: Uzbekistan is now one of ten countries participating in the Transformation Pathways Initiative (TPI), an international climate investment program totaling $720 million. Launched at COP31 in Turkey, the initiative aims to provide developing nations with long-term climate finance for adopting green technologies and reducing emissions.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Expand Cooperation in Youth Sphere
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia are enhancing cooperation in youth affairs, with discussions held in Tashkent between the head of Rossotrudnichestvo and local students. Key topics included educational collaboration, Russian language learning, and joint youth projects. Both sides agreed to establish interaction between youth parliamentary structures.

item.title: Combating Climate Change: Our Responsibility to Future Generations
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's initiatives at the UN climate change conference highlight the urgency of environmental security and sustainable development. The focus is on implementing green economy principles, increasing renewable energy use, reducing emissions, and efficient water resource management, particularly addressing the Aral Sea ecological crisis.

item.title: Uzbekistan and China Hold Business Forum to Boost Investment and Trade
item.description: A joint business forum between Uzbekistan and China, organized by the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Uzbekistan and Hainan province, took place in Tashkent. The event aimed to enhance trade and economic cooperation, attract foreign investment, and create a favorable business environment. Discussions focused on current trade relations and future collaboration opportunities.

item.title: US Congress Summons Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang for Testimony on National Security Concerns
item.description: The US Senate Banking Committee has invited Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to testify regarding national security concerns and the protection of critical technologies. Several House committees have also requested his appearance. Huang was asked to respond by November 13, with a closed-door meeting potentially scheduled for December 1.

item.title: IMF Recognizes Uzbekistan's Potential as Central Asia's Trade and Logistics Hub
item.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has identified Uzbekistan's significant potential to become a leading trade and logistics hub in Central Asia. Its favorable geographic location and strengthened regional economic ties are key factors. The IMF representative noted that this development would boost regional trade, attract investment, and enhance economic connectivity between Asian and European markets.

item.title: Uzbekistan Combats Tuberculosis with Modern Diagnostics, Dispelling Myths
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively working to control tuberculosis, countering the misconception that it is hereditary. Health specialists emphasize that TB is highly contagious and spreads through close contact, not genetics. While global TB mortality and incidence have decreased, challenges remain in detection and treatment, requiring continued efforts in Uzbekistan and worldwide.

item.title: Heads of Kazakhstan's Largest Sovereign Wealth Fund and National Company Arrested on Corruption Charges
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee announced the arrest of Nurlan Jakupov, head of the Samruk-Kazyna fund, and Yelyas Otinshiyev, head of Kazakhstan Temir Zholy, on suspicion of corruption. Both were detained on November 11. Investigations are ongoing to determine all circumstances of the case.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Prioritize Digital Control and Transparency in 2027 Budget, Says Saida Mirziyoyeva
item.description: Uzbekistan's government will focus on budget transparency and digital control for the upcoming year's expenditures, according to Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration. Key tax rates will remain unchanged. The largest portion of the budget will be allocated to education, healthcare, and local community development, aiming for 7% GDP growth.

item.title: Kazakh President Tasks National Security Committee Chairman on Key Issues
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Ермек Сағымбаев, Chairman of the National Security Committee (KNB). The KNB chairman reported on the committee's activities since the beginning of the year, including efforts against terrorism, extremism, drug trafficking, and organized crime. Special attention was given to anti-corruption and cybersecurity measures. The President issued several directives.

item.title: Khiva to Host UNESCO International Symposium on Cultural Heritage Preservation in 2027
item.description: UNESCO's Executive Board has supported holding an international symposium in Khiva in 2027 on "Preservation of Cultural Heritage in the Context of Globalization and Climate Change." The event will gather experts to discuss threats to cultural heritage, modern technologies, and traditional knowledge. Recommendations for improving heritage protection methods will be developed.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Attract $65 Billion in Foreign Investment by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to attract $65 billion in foreign investment by 2027, according to President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The country is developing a strategy for key sectors like chemical, petrochemical, mechanical engineering, and pharmaceuticals. Plans include attracting major international companies, establishing industrial zones, and deepening localization.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Orders Banks to Refund Illegal Loan Interest and Fines
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has mandated commercial banks to conduct internal audits by December 10th. Banks must identify and rectify legal violations, refunding any illegally charged loan interest and fines to borrowers. This directive follows court decisions on unlawful charges.

item.title: Kazakh Flight Attendant Contracts Unknown Illness in Kuwait, Loses Recognition
item.description: A 25-year-old Kazakh flight attendant fell ill with an unknown disease after a flight from Nepal to Kuwait. Initially recovering, her condition worsened, leading to memory loss and inability to recognize family. Kazakh diplomats assisted in her readmission to a clinic. Doctors are investigating potential causes, including Japanese encephalitis.

item.title: Sweden Shows Interest in Hiring Uzbek Citizens for Agriculture and Healthcare Sectors
item.description: Uzbekistan and Sweden are planning to enhance cooperation in vocational training to attract Uzbek specialists to the Swedish labor market. A forum in Stockholm discussed professional and language training for migrants and their legal employment abroad, highlighting Sweden's need for workers in agriculture, healthcare, and construction.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Enhanced CIS Cooperation in Emergency Prevention
item.description: Uzbekistan has proposed strengthening cooperation among CIS countries' emergency response agencies. The initiatives were presented at the 38th meeting of the Interstate Council for Emergency Situations in Shymkent. The focus is on shifting from emergency response to prevention and early risk detection, alongside modernizing technical capabilities and training.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Kurultai to Review Online Platform Content Liability Amendments
item.description: Kazakhstan's Kurultai will consider amendments establishing online platforms' liability for distributing destructive content and protecting children online. The Bureau approved the agenda, including new draft laws. The session will also review the 2027-2029 budget, international agreements with Singapore and Turkic states, and social security matters.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Main Tax Rates to Remain Unchanged in 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan's main tax rates will remain unchanged in 2027, according to Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of the Presidential Administration. This decision aims to support entrepreneurs and build a foundation for modern industry and job creation. The government also emphasized transparency in budget expenditures and digital control to ensure funds serve the public interest.

item.title: Uzbekistan Projects 7% Economic Growth by 2027, Inflation to Fall to 6%
item.description: Uzbekistan anticipates its economy to grow by 7% by 2027, reaching a GDP of $232 billion. Inflation is projected to decrease to 6% by 2027 and 5% by 2028-2029. The government aims to keep fiscal deficit within 3% of GDP and maintain current tax rates, focusing on economic activity stimulation and tax base expansion.

item.title: Kazakhstan Improves Drinking Water Supply in Langer Town
item.description: Langer town in Kazakhstan has improved its drinking water supply by repairing a well, costing 196.6 million tenge. This initiative fulfills President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's directive to ensure water access for remote settlements. The repaired well now supplies approximately 12,000 cubic meters of water daily, meeting the needs of 8,280 subscribers.

item.title: Iran Revives S-400 Missile System Purchase Talks with Russia
item.description: Iranian officials have once again raised the issue of purchasing S-400 anti-aircraft missile systems from Russia. Despite ongoing military-technical cooperation, the likelihood of reaching an agreement on the delivery of these systems is assessed as low. The article explores some of the reasons behind this.

item.title: US Central Command Denies Iranian Claims of Radar Destruction in Bahrain
item.description: US Central Command (CENTCOM) denied Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claims of destroying a US early warning radar at a military base in Bahrain. CENTCOM stated that two Iranian "suicide drones" were shot down en route to Bahrain and caused no casualties or damage.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Establishing Media Ombudsman to Protect Journalists
item.description: Uzbekistan is exploring the creation of an independent media ombudsman to safeguard the rights of journalists and media professionals. This initiative is part of a plan to improve the country's ranking in Reporters Without Borders' press freedom index. The plan also includes an open electronic registry of cases against journalists.

item.title: Tolebi District Completes Project to Provide Quality Drinking Water to Residents
item.description: The Tolebi District has completed a project to ensure quality drinking water for its residents. The "Dostyk-2" well underwent cleaning and repair, with the project costing 196.6 million tenge and finishing in December 2025. The regional governor emphasized the importance of this task, as assigned by the head of state.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims to Attract $65 Billion in Foreign Investment by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to attract $65 billion in foreign investment by 2027 and achieve at least 7% annual economic growth. The strategy includes a new growth model, high value-added production, increased labor productivity, and export potential expansion. Priority sectors like chemical, mechanical engineering, and pharmaceuticals will attract international companies.

item.title: Kazakhstan's People's Council Discusses AI Tools for Learning Kazakh Language
item.description: Kazakhstan's People's Council convened to discuss strengthening social cohesion, expanding the use of the state language, and developing digital technologies. Proposals included integrating artificial intelligence tools for learning Kazakh. The council adopted a joint action plan focusing on implementing the President's address and tasks set by the International "Qazaq Tili" Society. Participants also shared initiatives for promoting the state language in regions and preserving linguistic diversity.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan National Security Committee Denies Resort Transfer, Cites Investor Compensation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (GKNB) clarified that the 'Novel' resort in Korumdu village was not transferred to its balance. The GKNB stated that in a criminal case involving misappropriation of foreign investor assets, the damage was fully compensated by transferring the investor's share in the company owning the resort. Thus, the resort became part of the company's assets, which were transferred to the victim as compensation.

item.title: Microsoft Services Outage Affects Millions Globally, Entering Second Day
item.description: A widespread outage of Microsoft services has entered its second day, disrupting communications for companies, government agencies, courts, police, and public services in over 70 countries. Services like Outlook, Microsoft Teams, and Copilot were impacted. Microsoft reported progress in restoring services, particularly in North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific, though intermittent disruptions may persist.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Increase Education and Healthcare Funding by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to increase funding for education and healthcare by 2027, allocating approximately 176 trillion Uzbek soums in total. Next year, education expenditures are projected to rise by 14 trillion soums, and healthcare by 12 trillion soums. An additional 70 trillion soums will be directed towards regional infrastructure and social protection.

item.title: Turkmen Woman Jailed for Seven Years After Accusing Husband of Abuse
item.description: Jeren Altyeva, a resident of Bayramali, has been sentenced to seven years in prison after publicly accusing her ex-husband, a high-ranking official, of raping her and sexually harassing their daughter. Turkmen.news believes the case is fabricated by the Ministry of National Security in retaliation for her speaking out. Altyeva claims authorities covered up for her ex-husband due to his status.

item.title: Central Asia and Caucasus Face Growing Water Security Challenges, ADB Analysis Warns
item.description: An Asian Development Bank analysis highlights accelerating glacier melt in Central Asia and the Caucasus, warning of increased risks of drought, landslides, and glacial lake outburst floods. Average temperatures could rise by up to 5°C by 2085, impacting water availability and storage.

item.title: Turkmenistan Poised to Complete Section of TAPI Pipeline by End of 2026
item.description: Turkmenistan aims to complete a section of the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India (TAPI) pipeline by the end of 2026, stretching from the Turkmen border to Herat, Afghanistan. Approximately 80% of the route is prepared, with welding and hydrostatic testing underway.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans Three Nuclear Power Plants, Secures Uranium Reserves for 100 Years
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to build three nuclear power plants to meet growing electricity demands and establish a nuclear industry cluster. The country, second globally in uranium reserves and a major producer, views uranium as a strategic resource for energy and economic development. Plans also include training specialists and developing nuclear technologies for medicine and agriculture.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Maintain Key Tax Rates Unchanged Through 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan intends to keep its main tax rates unchanged through 2027. The state budget for the upcoming year is projected to have revenues of 416 trillion soums and expenditures of 464 trillion soums. The inflation target is set at no more than 6%.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry to Investigate Alleged Hacker Involvement in Tajikistan Cyberattack
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Digital Development will examine claims linking hackers from the country to a cyberattack on Tajikistan. Over two thousand government documents were reportedly stolen. The ministry stated that current data is insufficient to confirm any national involvement and will request research materials for verification.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Orders Review of Cases Affecting Innocent Businesspeople
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has ordered a review of cases where innocent businesspeople were allegedly harmed during anti-organized crime operations. He acknowledged that some individuals, possibly 10-15%, were wrongly implicated. The president's directive came after a resident complained about her husband being entrapped and pressured to forfeit property.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Halt Operations at Some Uranium Fields for Strategic Reserve
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to create a strategic reserve of uranium to meet domestic needs, temporarily suspending operations at certain fields. The Atomic Energy Agency stated this is linked to developing nuclear energy and rising global demand. Some finished uranium products will also be stored, with reserves established at each nuclear power plant for continuous operation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Warns Against Attempts to Destabilize Country Ahead of Elections
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov warned against political forces attempting to disrupt stability and prevent upcoming elections. He specifically mentioned a plot to incite ethnic Uzbek-Kyrgyz conflict to postpone the vote. Japarov assured that law enforcement has the capacity to maintain order and called for unity among all citizens living in Kyrgyzstan.
